datasets_evaluated.evidence: We evaluate the proposed I2RNN on two public datasets CIC-IDS2017 dataset [48] and ISCXVPN2016 traffic dataset [49], respectively.

label_source.evidence: The first dataset contains the hybrid of encrypted and unencrypted network traffic across five days, which can be divided into 8 classes

label_feature_overlap.evidence: The traffic classification in this paper refers to classifying the encrypted traffic of sessions into specific traffic types with raw features of packets.

features_used.evidence: Each packet feature vector consists of packet length, direction, the interval of arrival time, and values of fields in the packet header, e.g., TTL (Time To Live), TCP flags, and TCP window size.

feature_groups.evidence: The feature tensors are extracted from the first T packets in each session and are composed of the packet feature vectors.

fingerprints_used.evidence: The I2RNN leverages fingerprint learning from the raw session sequences rather than manually designed features.

tls_versions_stated.evidence: The applications are encrypted with various security protocols, including HTTPS, SSH, and proprietary protocols.

model_family.evidence: In this paper, we propose I2RNN, an Incremental and Interpretable Recurrent Neural Network for encrypted traffic classification.

split_protocols.evidence: We evaluate I2RNN and baseline classification methods with the 5-fold cross-validation.

main_split.evidence: We evaluate I2RNN and baseline classification methods with the 5-fold cross-validation.

easy_vs_hard_reported.evidence: We evaluate I2RNN and baseline classification methods with the 5-fold cross-validation.

metrics.evidence: We evaluate the classification performance of I2RNN with other baselines in terms of Accuracy (AC), Precision (PR), Recall (RC), and F1-Score (F1).

granularity.evidence: Each session is a sample and is composed of bi-directional packets with the same IP, port, and transport layer protocol.

first_n_packets.evidence: The time sequence length of each LSTM unit is set as 32.
